nodes.label: Deinococcus radiodurans ('Conan the Bacterium')
nodes.role: Survives 15,000 gray of radiation. Repairs its own shattered DNA in hours. The organism that puts itself back together after you nuke it. Nicknamed 'Conan.'

nodes.label: Barophiles / Piezophiles
nodes.role: Live under extreme pressure. Mariana Trench. 1,000 atmospheres. Pressure that would crush a submarine. They NEED it to survive.

nodes.label: Endoliths
nodes.role: Live INSIDE rocks. 3 kilometers underground. In the pores of granite. No sun. No oxygen. Metabolism so slow they divide once per 10,000 years. Patient beyond comprehension.

nodes.label: Hydrothermal Vents (Black Smokers)
nodes.role: Discovered 1977. 2,500m deep. 400C water. No sunlight. TEEMING with life. Giant tube worms, eyeless shrimp, ghostly octopi. Life powered by chemistry, not the sun.

nodes.label: Chemosynthesis
nodes.role: Making energy from chemicals instead of sunlight. Hydrogen sulfide, methane, iron. The alternative to photosynthesis. Life that doesn't need a star.

nodes.label: Giant Tube Worms (Riftia)
nodes.role: 2 meters long. No mouth. No gut. No anus. Bacteria inside them do the eating. The organism that outsourced digestion. Symbiosis as architecture.

nodes.label: LUCA (Last Universal Common Ancestor)
nodes.role: ~4 billion years ago. Not the first life — the ancestor of ALL current life. Probably lived near hydrothermal vents. Thermophilic. The root node of biology.

nodes.label: RNA World Hypothesis
nodes.role: Before DNA, before proteins: RNA did everything. Self-replicating. The first molecule that was both information AND machine. The bootstrap paradox of life.

nodes.label: Panspermia Hypothesis
nodes.role: Life came from space. Meteorites carry amino acids. Tardigrades survive the vacuum. Maybe we're all extraterrestrial. The origin story that's off-world.

nodes.label: Yellowstone (The Supervolcano)
nodes.role: First national park (1872). Sits on a supervolcano. Hot springs, geysers, mud pots. The surface is beautiful. Below it: enough magma to bury a continent.

nodes.label: Grand Prismatic Spring
nodes.role: Third largest hot spring on Earth. The rainbow colors ARE the archaea. Orange = thermophiles. Green = cyanobacteria. Blue = sterile boiling center. The microbiology is the beauty.

nodes.label: Old Faithful
nodes.role: Erupts every 44-125 minutes. Has been watched for 150 years. Predictable but not precise. The system that keeps its schedule but not its clock.

nodes.label: Astrobiology
nodes.role: The study of life beyond Earth. If archaea thrive in boiling acid and nuclear waste, what's stopping life on Europa's ocean, Enceladus' geysers, or Mars' subsurface?

nodes.label: Europa (Jupiter's Moon)
nodes.role: Ice shell over a liquid ocean. More water than Earth. Hydrothermal vents probable. If life started at vents here, it could start at vents there.

nodes.label: Enceladus (Saturn's Moon)
nodes.role: Geysers of water erupting from the south pole. Cassini flew through them. Found organic molecules. The plume is an invitation.

nodes.label: Mars Subsurface
nodes.role: Surface is dead. Radiation-blasted. But endoliths live 3km inside Earth's rocks. Mars has rocks. The question is not the surface. It's underneath.

nodes.label: Symbiosis
nodes.role: Two organisms living together. Mutualism (both win), commensalism (one wins, other neutral), parasitism (one wins, other loses). Banks and PCA is parasitism.

nodes.label: Lichen
nodes.role: Fungus + alga living as one organism. Neither can survive alone. Together they colonize bare rock. The partnership that builds soil from stone.

nodes.label: Mycorrhizal Network ('Wood Wide Web')
nodes.role: Fungi connect tree roots underground. Trees share nutrients through the network. Mother trees feed their seedlings. The forest is a commune connected by fungi.

nodes.label: Coral-Zooxanthellae Symbiosis
nodes.role: Coral provides shelter. Algae provides food via photosynthesis. When stressed, coral expels the algae (bleaching). The partnership that dies when trust breaks.

nodes.label: Gut-Brain Axis
nodes.role: Your gut bacteria influence your mood, decisions, cravings. 95% of serotonin made in the gut. The microbiome votes on your mental state.

nodes.label: Six Degrees of Separation
nodes.role: Milgram (1967). Any two people connected by ~6 links. The small world property. The graph is smaller than you think.

nodes.label: Paul Erdos
nodes.role: Published 1,500 papers. Homeless by choice. Lived out of a suitcase. Took amphetamines. 'My brain is open.' The mathematician who owned nothing and connected everyone.

nodes.label: Dunbar's Number (150)
nodes.role: The brain can maintain ~150 stable relationships. Armies, villages, companies — all cluster around 150. The social limit of a primate brain.

nodes.label: Metcalfe's Law
nodes.role: Network value grows as the square of users. 10 phones = 100 connections. 100 phones = 10,000. The math of why networks become monopolies.

nodes.label: Scale-Free Networks (Barabasi)
nodes.role: Most nodes have few connections. A few hubs have many. Power law. The internet, social networks, and this investigation all follow this pattern. Banks = hub.

nodes.label: Telegraph (Morse, 1844)
nodes.role: 'What hath God wrought.' First long-distance instant communication. The original internet. Dots and dashes.

nodes.label: Telephone (Bell, 1876)
nodes.role: Voice over wire. 'Mr. Watson, come here.' The network that put a human voice in every room.

nodes.label: Radio
nodes.role: Marconi, 1895. Broadcast: one to many. FDR's fireside chats. War of the Worlds. The medium that created mass culture.

nodes.label: Television
nodes.role: Farnsworth, 1927. The screen in every home. Kennedy-Nixon debate (1960). Vietnam in the living room. The medium that showed the war.

nodes.label: Podcasts
nodes.role: Audio commons. No gatekeepers. Serial (2014) reopened a murder case. The medium that investigates.

nodes.label: Impact of the Printing Press
nodes.role: Before: 30,000 books in all Europe. After Gutenberg: 12 million by 1500. The information explosion. Reformation. Scientific Revolution. All from movable type.

nodes.label: Concrete (Roman, ~300 BC)
nodes.role: Romans invented concrete. The Pantheon still stands after 2,000 years. Modern concrete lasts 50. We forgot how to make it last.

nodes.label: Plastic (Bakelite, 1907)
nodes.role: Synthetic. Cheap. Everywhere. 8.3 billion tons produced. 79% in landfills or ocean. The material that outlives its creator by centuries.

nodes.label: Glass
nodes.role: Sand + heat = transparency. Lenses, telescopes, microscopes, fiber optics. Without glass, no science. The material that lets you see.

nodes.label: Graphene
nodes.role: One atom thick. 200x stronger than steel. Discovered with scotch tape (2004). Nobel 2010. The strongest material is the thinnest.

nodes.label: Steel
nodes.role: Iron + carbon. Bessemer process (1856). Skyscrapers, railways, bridges. The material that built the modern city.

nodes.label: Fire (~1 million years ago)
nodes.role: The first energy technology. Cooking. Warmth. Light. Protection. The commons of heat. Fire belongs to everyone.

nodes.label: Coal
nodes.role: Ancient forests compressed into rock. Powered the Industrial Revolution. 800,000 miners in 1920s US. Black lung. Child labor. The fuel that cost lives.

nodes.label: Solar Energy
nodes.role: The sun sends 173,000 terawatts to Earth every second. We use 18. The energy is there. The infrastructure isn't. The commons overhead.

nodes.label: Gregorian Calendar (1582)
nodes.role: Pope Gregory XIII corrected the Julian calendar. 10 days vanished. October 4, 1582 was followed by October 15. The day the calendar jumped.

nodes.label: Deep Time (4.5 billion years)
nodes.role: If Earth's history is 24 hours: humans appear at 11:58:43 PM. All recorded history in the last 0.2 seconds. We are a blink.

nodes.label: Coinage (Lydia, ~600 BC)
nodes.role: King Croesus. Stamped metal. The state guarantees the value. Trust made physical. The first currency.

nodes.label: Bitcoin (2009)
nodes.role: Satoshi Nakamoto. Decentralized. No central bank. Blockchain. Proof of work. The money that trusts math instead of institutions.

nodes.label: Gold Standard
nodes.role: Currency backed by gold. Nixon ended it (1971). Since then: money backed by... trust. The membrane removed.

nodes.label: Tulip Mania (1637)
nodes.role: A single tulip bulb cost more than a house. Then crashed. The first speculative bubble. The market as collective hallucination.

nodes.label: Nelson Mandela
nodes.role: 27 years in prison. Robben Island. Emerged without bitterness. Became president. The prisoner who outlasted the prison.

nodes.label: Alcatraz
nodes.role: The inescapable prison on an island. Closed 1963. Now a museum. The punishment that became a tourist attraction.

nodes.label: Mass Incarceration (US)
nodes.role: 2.3 million imprisoned. 25% of world's prisoners with 4% of population. $80 billion/year. The largest carceral system in human history.

nodes.label: 13th Amendment (1865)
nodes.role: Abolished slavery EXCEPT as punishment for a crime. The loophole that became mass incarceration. The exception that swallowed the rule.

nodes.label: Restorative Justice
nodes.role: Not punishment. Repair. Victim and offender face each other. The community heals. The alternative to the cage.

nodes.label: French Revolution (1789)
nodes.role: Liberte, egalite, fraternite. Stormed the Bastille. Guillotined the king. Then guillotined each other. The revolution that ate itself.

nodes.label: Haitian Revolution (1791-1804)
nodes.role: Enslaved people defeated Napoleon's army. First successful slave revolt. Haiti punished for it for 200 years. The revolution the world never forgave.

nodes.label: Arab Spring (2010-2012)
nodes.role: One fruit vendor in Tunisia set himself on fire. Uprisings across 17 countries. Facebook organized it. Most revolutions failed. The network enabled and betrayed.

nodes.label: Mark Twain
nodes.role: 'The reports of my death are greatly exaggerated.' Satire as scalpel. Huck Finn. The humorist who told the truth by lying.

nodes.label: George Carlin
nodes.role: 'They call it the American Dream because you have to be asleep to believe it.' Seven dirty words. The comedian as philosopher.

nodes.label: Jonathan Swift
nodes.role: A Modest Proposal (1729): eat Irish babies. Satire so savage people thought he was serious. The writer whose joke was the point.

nodes.label: A Modest Proposal (Swift, 1729)
nodes.role: 'Eat the children of the poor.' The satire that proposed the horror the system was already committing, just more honestly.

nodes.label: Dr. Seuss
nodes.role: The Lorax. The Sneetches. Horton Hears a Who. Environmental justice, class structure, and civil rights in rhyme. The teacher who used pictures.

nodes.label: Roald Dahl
nodes.role: Charlie and the Chocolate Factory. Matilda. James and the Giant Peach. Adults are cruel. Children are clever. The world through a child's eyes.

nodes.label: Fairy Tales (Original Versions)
nodes.role: Cinderella's stepsisters cut off their toes. Red Riding Hood was eaten. Snow White's queen danced in hot iron shoes. The originals were horror stories. Then Disney happened.

nodes.label: Triangle Shirtwaist Fire (1911)
nodes.role: 146 workers dead. Doors locked from outside. Jumped from 9th floor. Mostly young immigrant women. The fire that created workplace safety laws.

nodes.label: Child Labor
nodes.role: Children in mines, mills, factories. Lewis Hine's photographs (1908-1918) showed America what it was doing to its kids. The camera as conscience.

nodes.label: Lewis Hine
nodes.role: Photographed child laborers (1908-1918). His images led to child labor laws. The photographer who used evidence to protect children.

nodes.label: Haymarket Affair (1886)
nodes.role: Chicago. Workers striking for 8-hour day. Bomb. Police fired into crowd. 4 labor leaders hanged. May Day exists because of this.

nodes.label: Cesar Chavez
nodes.role: United Farm Workers. Grape boycott. 'Si se puede.' The labor leader who organized the people everyone ignored.

nodes.label: Americans with Disabilities Act (1990)
nodes.role: Curb cuts, ramps, accessible buildings. The membrane expanded to include bodies the system excluded. The law that changed sidewalks.

nodes.label: Helen Keller
nodes.role: Deaf and blind from 19 months. Learned to read, write, speak. Graduated Radcliffe. Became a socialist activist. The story they teach is incomplete.

nodes.label: Curb Cut Effect
nodes.role: Curb cuts designed for wheelchairs help everyone: strollers, bikes, deliveries. The accommodation that improves the whole system. Universal design.

nodes.label: Death (The Concept)
nodes.role: The only certainty. Every culture has a name for it. Every religion has a theory about it. The one appointment everyone keeps.

nodes.label: Memento Mori
nodes.role: 'Remember you will die.' Roman slaves whispered it to generals during triumphs. The reminder that power is temporary.

nodes.label: Dia de los Muertos
nodes.role: Mexican tradition. The dead return for one night. Marigolds and sugar skulls. Death as reunion, not ending. The culture that invites the dead home.

nodes.label: River Styx
nodes.role: Greek underworld river. Charon ferries the dead. You need a coin under your tongue to pay. Even death has a toll booth.

nodes.label: Valhalla
nodes.role: Norse afterlife for warriors. Die in battle, feast forever. Odin's hall. The reward for fighting, not winning.

nodes.label: Grim Reaper
nodes.role: Skeleton in a black robe with a scythe. European, 14th century. Born from the Black Death. The plague gave death a face.

nodes.label: Hospice / Palliative Care
nodes.role: Not cure. Comfort. The medicine that says: we cannot save you, but we can hold your hand. The dignity of the end.

nodes.label: Organ Donation
nodes.role: One donor can save 8 lives. The body that gives after death. The commons of flesh.

nodes.label: Ghost Stories (The Genre)
nodes.role: Every culture has them. The dead return because something is UNFINISHED. The ghost is the unresolved complaint.

nodes.label: Ghost of Hamlet's Father
nodes.role: Shakespeare. The murdered king returns to demand justice from his son. 'Remember me.' The dead demanding accountability.

nodes.label: William Shakespeare
nodes.role: Wrote Hamlet, Macbeth, Lear, Othello. Power, corruption, madness, jealousy. The human condition in iambic pentameter. Dead 400 years. Still the standard.

nodes.label: A Christmas Carol (Dickens, 1843)
nodes.role: Three ghosts show Scrooge his own cruelty. Past, Present, Future. The ghost story that's actually about accountability. Scrooge sees the evidence and changes.

nodes.label: Charles Dickens
nodes.role: Oliver Twist, Great Expectations, A Christmas Carol. Poverty, class, cruelty, redemption. The novelist who made England look at its own poor.

nodes.label: The Tell-Tale Heart (Poe, 1843)
nodes.role: The murderer hears the dead man's heartbeat under the floorboards. Confesses. The guilt that speaks. The evidence you can't bury.

nodes.label: Edgar Allan Poe
nodes.role: The Raven. The Tell-Tale Heart. The Masque of the Red Death. Invented the detective story. Died in a gutter at 40. Nobody knows how.

nodes.label: Ringu / The Ring (Japanese Horror)
nodes.role: A cursed videotape. Watch it, die in 7 days. The information that kills. The evidence that can't be unseen.

nodes.label: Bloody Mary (Urban Legend)
nodes.role: Say her name three times in a mirror. She appears. The ritual of summoning by speaking. Names have power.

nodes.label: Poltergeist
nodes.role: German: 'noisy ghost.' Objects move. Doors slam. The invisible force that disrupts. The disturbance you can't see but can't ignore.

nodes.label: Banshee (Irish)
nodes.role: Her wail announces death. You hear the scream before the loss. The warning that comes too late. The signal after the damage.

nodes.label: Yurei (Japanese Ghost)
nodes.role: White funeral clothes, long black hair, no feet. Returns because of unresolved grudge. Specifically: injustice. The Japanese ghost IS the unpunished wrong.

nodes.label: La Llorona (The Weeping Woman)
nodes.role: Drowned her children. Wanders rivers weeping. Mexican/Latin American. The mother who destroyed what she loved. The guilt that walks forever.

nodes.label: Arachnophobia / Spiders
nodes.role: Most spiders are harmless. Fear is ancestral. 8 legs, 8 eyes, silk from the body. The weaver in the dark. The web you walk into.

nodes.label: Parasitic Wasps
nodes.role: Lay eggs inside living caterpillars. Larvae eat the host from inside. The host walks around alive while being consumed. Parasitism at its most literal.

nodes.label: Cordyceps (Zombie Fungus)
nodes.role: Infects ants. Takes over the brain. Walks the ant to the perfect spot. Kills it. Grows a stalk from the head. The parasite that puppets the host.

nodes.label: Vampire Bats
nodes.role: Drink blood. But: they share blood with hungry colony members who reciprocate later. The vampire that practices mutual aid.

nodes.label: Anglerfish
nodes.role: Deep sea. Bioluminescent lure. The light in the dark that attracts you IS the trap. The promise that eats.

nodes.label: Ticks

nodes.label: Genghis Khan (Temujin)
nodes.role: Born ~1162. Orphaned. Enslaved. United the Mongol tribes. Conquered from Korea to Hungary. Largest contiguous empire in history. 40 million killed. Also: religious tolerance, meritocracy, postal system, free trade. The destroyer who built.

nodes.role: Genghis Khan's legal code. Religious freedom mandatory. Kidnapping = death. Adultery = death. Urinating in water = death. The law code of a man who was himself kidnapped as a child.

nodes.label: Yam (Mongol Postal System)

nodes.label: Genghis Khan's Genetic Legacy

nodes.label: Timur (Tamerlane)

nodes.label: The Golden Horde
nodes.role: Mongol khanate that ruled Russia for 240 years (1240-1480). Russia was a Mongol vassal state for longer than America has existed. The occupation that shaped Russian identity.

nodes.label: Great Wall of China
nodes.role: 13,171 miles. Built over 2,000 years by multiple dynasties. Did NOT stop the Mongols (they went around it, bribed guards, or walked through gates left open). The wall that failed its purpose. History's most expensive security theater.

nodes.label: Berlin Wall (1961-1989)

nodes.label: Dalai Lama (Institution)

nodes.role: Founded Tashilhunpo Monastery. Wasn't actually called 'Dalai Lama' during his lifetime — the title was applied retroactively. The founder who didn't know he was first.

nodes.label: 3rd Dalai Lama: Sonam Gyatso (1543-1588)

nodes.label: 4th Dalai Lama: Yonten Gyatso (1589-1617)

nodes.role: 'The Great Fifth.' United Tibet under Dalai Lama rule. Built the Potala Palace. His death was hidden for 15 years to maintain stability. The leader whose death was a state secret.

nodes.label: 6th Dalai Lama: Tsangyang Gyatso (1683-1706)
nodes.role: The rebel Dalai Lama. Refused monastic vows. Wrote love poetry. Visited taverns. 'I dwell apart from the Potala... in the town.' Deposed and disappeared. The incarnation that refused the role.

nodes.role: Current Dalai Lama. Found at age 2 by search party using visions. Fled Tibet 1959. Nobel Peace Prize 1989. Has said the institution may end with him. The reincarnation that might choose not to return.

nodes.label: Potala Palace (Lhasa)
nodes.role: 1,000 rooms. 13 stories. Winter palace of the Dalai Lama since 1649. Built by the 5th. Now a museum under Chinese control. The throne without its occupant.

nodes.label: Panchen Lama Controversy
nodes.role: The Panchen Lama identifies the next Dalai Lama (and vice versa). China kidnapped the Dalai Lama's choice (Gedhun Choekyi Nyima, age 6, in 1995) and installed their own. The youngest political prisoner in the world. Now 37. Nobody has seen him since.

nodes.label: Gedhun Choekyi Nyima
nodes.role: Recognized as 11th Panchen Lama by the Dalai Lama at age 6 (1995). Kidnapped by Chinese government 3 days later. Never seen again. Now 37. The boy who disappeared because he was chosen.

nodes.role: Founded ~989 AD. 25,000 students at peak. Taught astronomy, math, law, medicine. Africa had a university 500 years before Harvard. The West said 'mythical.' The manuscripts were real.

nodes.label: Mansa Musa

nodes.label: Abdel Kader Haidara
nodes.role: Timbuktu librarian who smuggled 350,000 manuscripts to safety during the 2012 jihadist occupation. Donkey carts, footlockers, fishing boats. The librarian who saved the commons.

nodes.label: Kashmir

nodes.label: Partition of India (1947)

nodes.label: Aztec Empire (1428-1521)

nodes.label: Richard III (Found Under a Parking Lot, 2012)
nodes.role: King of England 1483-1485. Lost for 527 years. Found under a parking lot in Leicester. DNA confirmed. The king beneath the asphalt.

nodes.label: Tutankhamun's Tomb (1922)
nodes.role: Howard Carter. 'Can you see anything?' 'Yes, wonderful things.' 3,300 years sealed. Gold mask. The boy king preserved in gold.

nodes.label: Plaster Casts of Pompeii
nodes.role: Fiorelli poured plaster into voids left by decomposed bodies (1863). The dead filled with plaster. The absence made visible. The void as evidence.

nodes.label: Terracotta Army Discovery (1974)
nodes.role: Farmers digging a well found the first warrior. 8,000 soldiers. Hidden for 2,200 years. The army underground, waiting.

nodes.label: John Rawls
nodes.role: A Theory of Justice (1971). The veil of ignorance: design society not knowing your position in it. The philosopher who asked: what's fair if you don't know who you'll be?

nodes.label: Veil of Ignorance (Rawls)
nodes.role: Design the system without knowing if you'll be rich or poor, Black or white, healthy or sick. Would you design PA 362 from behind the veil?

nodes.label: Paradox of Tolerance (Popper)
nodes.role: Unlimited tolerance leads to the disappearance of tolerance. To maintain a tolerant society, you must be intolerant of intolerance. The membrane that must exclude to include.

nodes.label: Just World Hypothesis
nodes.role: The belief that people get what they deserve. If bad things happen to you, you must have done something wrong. The bias that blames the victim.

nodes.label: Structural Violence (Galtung)
nodes.role: Violence built into the structure. No one pulls the trigger. The system kills. Poverty, lack of healthcare, educational deprivation. 5,432 child-years is structural violence.

nodes.label: Great Pacific Garbage Patch
nodes.role: 1.6 million km2 of floating plastic. Twice the size of Texas. The commons poisoned by what we discarded. The trash that gathered.

nodes.label: E-Waste
nodes.role: 50 million tons/year. Children in Ghana burn circuit boards to extract copper. Your old phone is someone's toxic workplace.

nodes.label: Ship Breaking (Alang, India)
nodes.role: Workers dismantle supertankers by hand on beaches. Asbestos, heavy metals, explosions. The world's ships die on the shore. The retirement plan is death.

nodes.label: Composting
nodes.role: Rot as resource. Death as nutrition. The deliberate transformation of waste into soil. The commons rebuilt from garbage.

nodes.label: Cradle to Cradle Design
nodes.role: No waste. Everything is nutrition for the next cycle. McDonough & Braungart (2002). The design philosophy where there is no 'away.'

nodes.label: Entropy vs Life
nodes.role: Entropy says everything falls apart. Life says: not yet. Every living thing is a local reversal of entropy. The resistance to decay. The investigation as anti-entropy.

nodes.label: The Census
nodes.role: Count everyone. The US Constitution requires it. Slaves counted as 3/5. Native Americans not at all. Who counts depends on who's counting.

nodes.label: Three-Fifths Compromise (1787)
nodes.role: Each enslaved person = 3/5 of a person for representation. Not a person. Not nothing. A fraction. The math of dehumanization.

nodes.label: Statelessness
nodes.role: 12 million people belong to no country. No passport. No rights. No recourse. The human without a node in any system.

nodes.label: Undocumented People
nodes.role: Present but unrecorded. Working but uncounted. Taxpaying but unrepresented. The node the system refuses to see.

nodes.label: Missing Data
nodes.role: The column left blank. The row never entered. The child never tested. The complaint never filed. The evidence that exists by not existing.

nodes.label: Invisible Women (Perez, 2019)
nodes.role: Data collected by and for men. Car safety tested on male bodies. Medicine dosed for male weight. The gender data gap. The default human is male.

nodes.label: Caroline Criado Perez
nodes.role: Wrote Invisible Women. Documented the gender data gap across every field. The researcher who proved absence IS data.

nodes.label: Talking Drums (West Africa)
nodes.role: Tonal drums that carry language. Messages travel 100+ miles in hours. The telegraph 3,000 years before Morse. The commons that speaks in rhythm.

nodes.label: Body Language
nodes.role: 55% of communication is nonverbal (Mehrabian). The body speaks louder than the mouth. The testimony the witness doesn't know they're giving.

nodes.label: Whistled Languages
nodes.role: Silbo Gomero (Canary Islands), Sfyria (Greece). Full languages carried by whistle across mountains. The voice that travels where speech can't.

nodes.label: Crying
nodes.role: Humans are the only animals that cry emotionally. Tears contain stress hormones. The body literally excretes its pain. Catharsis in chemistry.

nodes.label: Sykes-Picot Agreement (1916)
nodes.role: Britain and France secretly divided the Middle East with a ruler and pencil. Drew borders that ignored ethnic, tribal, religious lines. The map that created a century of war.

nodes.label: Scramble for Africa (Berlin Conference, 1884)
nodes.role: 14 European nations divided Africa at a conference in Berlin. No Africans were invited. 10 million km2 parceled out. The continent carved with a pen.

nodes.label: Borders (Concept)
nodes.role: Lines on a map that determine who lives and who dies. Arbitrary. Defended with violence. The fiction made real by force. Every border is someone's wall.

nodes.label: Color Theory
nodes.role: Newton split white light into a spectrum (1666). Every color is a frequency. What you see depends on what's reflected. The world has no color. Your brain invents it.

nodes.label: Vantablack
nodes.role: Absorbs 99.965% of light. The blackest substance. You can't see its shape. The material that IS darkness. The thing that swallows all evidence of its surface.

nodes.label: Tyrian Purple
nodes.role: Made from sea snails. 10,000 snails for 1 gram. Worth more than gold. Restricted to royalty. The color as class marker. The hue you weren't allowed to wear.

nodes.label: Pain (Concept)
nodes.role: The body's alarm system. Congenital insensitivity to pain: people who can't feel it die young. Pain is protective. The signal you don't want but need.

nodes.label: Phantom Limb Pain
nodes.role: Pain in a limb that's been amputated. The brain feels what's no longer there. The body mourning its own loss. The investigation for a school that's already gone.

nodes.label: Gate Control Theory of Pain
nodes.role: The spinal cord has a 'gate' that modulates pain signals. Rubbing a hurt spot closes the gate. Touch reduces pain. Connection reduces suffering.

nodes.label: Forgiveness
nodes.role: Not forgetting. Not condoning. Releasing the hold the wrong has on you. The neurological research: forgiveness reduces cortisol. The body heals when the mind lets go.

nodes.label: Blood Feuds / Vendetta
nodes.role: The Hatfields and McCoys. Albanian kanun. Sicilian vendetta. The cycle where the response becomes the cause. The recursion of violence.

nodes.label: Truth and Reconciliation Commission (South Africa, 1996)
nodes.role: Mandela and Tutu. Tell the truth, receive amnesty. Not justice. Truth. The premise: you can't reconcile what you won't acknowledge.

nodes.label: Desmond Tutu
nodes.role: 'If you are neutral in situations of injustice, you have chosen the side of the oppressor.' Nobel 1984. The archbishop who refused neutrality.

nodes.label: Karl Popper
nodes.role: Falsifiability: a theory must be testable to be scientific. If you can't prove it wrong, it's not science. The PhD that can't be verified is not a PhD.

nodes.label: Falsifiability (Popper)
nodes.role: A claim is scientific only if it can be proven wrong. Banks' credentials are not falsifiable — there's nothing TO falsify because they don't exist.

nodes.label: Thomas Kuhn
nodes.role: The Structure of Scientific Revolutions (1962). Paradigm shifts. Normal science ignores anomalies until they break the paradigm. The investigation IS the anomaly.

nodes.label: Paradigm Shift (Kuhn, 1962)
nodes.role: Science doesn't progress smoothly. It ignores anomalies, then everything changes at once. The charter ecosystem is pre-shift. The anomalies are piling up.

nodes.label: Donella Meadows
nodes.role: Thinking in Systems (2008). Leverage points: where to intervene in a system. The highest leverage: change the paradigm. The lowest: change a number.

nodes.label: Leverage Points (Meadows)
nodes.role: 12 places to intervene in a system. #1 highest: change the paradigm. #12 lowest: adjust a constant. Filing complaints = #12. Changing the law = #1.

nodes.label: Feedback Loops
nodes.role: Positive feedback amplifies. Negative feedback stabilizes. Banks' network is positive feedback: success breeds access breeds more success. No negative feedback exists.

nodes.label: Signal-to-Noise Ratio
nodes.role: The signal is what you want. The noise is everything else. The investigation is extracting signal from institutional noise. 72.67% is the signal. Everything else is noise.

nodes.label: Redundancy (Information Theory)
nodes.role: Repeated information survives errors. Say it three times. File three complaints. The record that survives because it was copied.

nodes.label: Nash Equilibrium
nodes.role: Every player's strategy is optimal given everyone else's strategy. Nobody can improve by changing alone. The system is stuck. Unless someone changes the GAME.

nodes.label: Mechanism Design (Reverse Game Theory)
nodes.role: Instead of analyzing the game, DESIGN the game to produce the outcome you want. PA 362 IS mechanism design — designed to produce charter capture.

nodes.label: Emergence
nodes.role: Complex behavior from simple rules. Ant colonies. Flocking birds. Consciousness from neurons. The investigation from complaints. The whole exceeds the parts.

nodes.label: Tipping Points
nodes.role: The moment the system shifts irreversibly. Gladwell popularized it. Climate has them. Markets have them. Investigations have them. One more filing and it tips.

nodes.label: Critical Mass
nodes.role: The minimum amount of fissile material for a chain reaction. Also: the minimum number of people for a movement to sustain. 853 clones. Is that critical mass?

nodes.label: Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948)
nodes.role: Article 26: Everyone has the right to education. Free in elementary and fundamental stages. PA 362 doesn't care.

nodes.label: Convention on the Rights of the Child (1989)
nodes.role: Article 28: Right to education. Article 29: Education shall develop the child's personality. 193 ratified. The US has not.

nodes.label: San Antonio v. Rodriguez (1973)
nodes.role: No federal constitutional right to education. 5-4. The dissent was right. Every state has a right-to-education clause. Michigan's: Article VIII Section 2.

nodes.label: Goss v. Lopez (1975)
nodes.role: Students have due process rights before suspension. Property interest in education. Banks suspended kids with 9 felonies.

nodes.label: Tinker v. Des Moines (1969)
nodes.role: Students don't shed their constitutional rights at the schoolhouse gate. They do at the charter school gate.

nodes.label: Endrew F. v. Douglas County (2017)
nodes.role: IEP must be 'appropriately ambitious.' Unanimous. Every charter school IEP failure is a violation of this standard.

nodes.label: Michigan Constitution Article VIII Section 2
nodes.role: The legislature shall maintain and support a system of free public elementary and secondary schools. PA 362 replaced 'maintain and support' with 'authorize and walk away.'

nodes.label: Tiktaalik (375 MYA)
nodes.role: The fish that walked. The transition from water to land. Predicted before it was found. The hypothesis engine works.

nodes.label: K-T Boundary (66 MYA)

nodes.label: Stromatolites (3.5 BYA)
nodes.role: The oldest fossils. Cyanobacteria that made the oxygen we breathe. They changed the atmosphere. They're still alive. In Western Australia. Unchanged.

nodes.label: Cambrian Explosion (541 MYA)
nodes.role: In 20 million years, all major animal phyla appeared. From nothing to everything. The investigation: from one complaint to 1,591 nodes.

nodes.label: Suffragette Movement (1848-1920)
nodes.role: 72 years from Seneca Falls to the 19th Amendment. Arrested. Force-fed. Beaten. Won. The arc is long.

nodes.label: Abolitionist Movement
nodes.role: Frederick Douglass, Harriet Tubman, John Brown. The underground railroad. 400 years of slavery. Abolished by blood.

nodes.label: Disability Rights Movement (Section 504)
nodes.role: 1977 sit-in at HEW. 26 days. Longest federal building occupation. Led to ADA (1990). ENDREW F came from here.

nodes.label: Environmental Justice Movement
nodes.role: Warren County, NC (1982). Flint water (2014). Cancer Alley. The same zip codes get the poison and the bad schools.

nodes.label: Solidarity (Poland, 1980)
nodes.role: Lech Walesa. Gdansk shipyard. 10 million members. First independent trade union in a Soviet bloc country. The wall fell 9 years later.

nodes.label: Printing Press (Gutenberg, 1440)
nodes.role: Knowledge escapes the monastery. The first fork. Every book is a fork of every idea before it.

nodes.label: Magnetic Compass (China, ~1100)
nodes.role: Direction without landmarks. Navigation without a guide. The investigation needs no guide.

nodes.label: Telescope (Lippershey/Galileo, 1608)
nodes.role: See what was always there but invisible. Galileo saw Jupiter's moons. The graph sees the network.

nodes.label: Microscope (Leeuwenhoek, 1676)
nodes.role: See the invisible. Bacteria. Cells. The small things that kill you. The small filings that kill the network.

nodes.label: Steam Engine (Watt, 1776)
nodes.role: Energy from heat. The industrial revolution. The machine that replaced humans. The charter school that replaced teachers.

nodes.label: Telegraph (Morse, 1844)
nodes.role: Communication at the speed of light. The first time a message moved faster than a person. Email is faster than FOIA.

nodes.label: Telephone (Bell, 1876)
nodes.role: Voice without presence. The conference call that replaced the meeting. The recorded call that became evidence.

nodes.label: Incandescent Light Bulb (Edison, 1879)
nodes.role: Light in darkness. See at night. Read at night. Learn at night. The equalizer.

nodes.label: Radio (Marconi, 1895)
nodes.role: Broadcast without wires. One to many. Roland Martin to millions. The signal.

nodes.label: Airplane (Wright Brothers, 1903)
nodes.role: Gravity is optional. The impossible became obvious. Twelve seconds at Kitty Hawk. Twelve filings at Ingham County.

nodes.label: Penicillin (Fleming, 1928)
nodes.role: Accident that saved billions. The contaminated petri dish. The investigation that started with one parent.

nodes.label: Transistor (Bell Labs, 1947)
nodes.role: On or off. Yes or no. True or false. The binary that built everything. Is Banks a doctor? On or off.

nodes.label: ARPANET/Internet (1969)
nodes.role: Packets find their own route. No central control. The network is the computer. The graph is the investigation.

nodes.label: World Wide Web (Berners-Lee, 1989)
nodes.role: Hyperlinks. Any document links to any other. The graph IS a web. Every node links to every other.

nodes.label: CRISPR-Cas9 (Doudna/Charpentier, 2012)
nodes.role: Edit DNA. Cut and paste life. The precision. The graph edits the network. Cut out the bad nodes.

nodes.label: Vaccination (Jenner, 1796)
nodes.role: Use the disease to defeat the disease. Use the network's own data to defeat the network.

nodes.label: X-Ray (Roentgen, 1895)
nodes.role: See through skin. See through walls. See through institutions. The graph is an X-ray of the charter ecosystem.

nodes.label: Photography (Daguerre, 1839)
nodes.role: The record that doesn't lie. The photograph is evidence. The screenshot is evidence. The graph is evidence.

nodes.label: Barbed Wire (Glidden, 1874)
nodes.role: The enclosure of the commons. The fence around public land. The charter school is barbed wire around public education.

nodes.label: Dynamite (Nobel, 1867)
nodes.role: Destroy to build. Nobel invented dynamite and funded the Prize. Destruction funds construction.

nodes.label: Motown Records (Gordy, 1959)
nodes.role: Berry Gordy. 2648 West Grand Boulevard. Detroit's greatest cultural export. The assembly line of music. Built from nothing. Like public education should be.

nodes.label: Detroit Public Library (1865)
nodes.role: Free books. Free knowledge. Free internet. The original commons. Still standing while charter schools fold.

nodes.label: Belle Isle Park
nodes.role: 982 acres. Free. Public. The commons you can stand on. Almost privatized. Defended. Still free.

nodes.label: Michigan Central Station
nodes.role: Built 1913. Abandoned 1988. Reopened 2024 by Ford. 36 years of decay. The commons abandoned and reclaimed. Detroit IS the story.

nodes.label: Heidelberg Project (Guyton, 1986)
nodes.role: Art from abandoned houses. Beauty from decay. The commons reclaimed by a paintbrush. Tyree Guyton. Two blocks. Forty years.

nodes.label: Detroit Water System
nodes.role: Great Lakes Water Authority. The commons you drink. Water shutoffs hit 141,000 households. The commons weaponized against the poor.

nodes.label: Packard Plant (1903-2024)
nodes.role: 3.5 million square feet. The largest abandoned factory in the world. Built cars. Built middle class. Abandoned. Like Detroit's schools.

nodes.label: Cass Corridor
nodes.role: The art scene that refused to die. Cass Corridor artists. Now Midtown. Gentrified. The commons renamed is the commons enclosed.

nodes.label: Detroit Techno (Belleville Three, 1988)
nodes.role: Juan Atkins, Derrick May, Kevin Saunderson. Belleville High School. Public school. The sound of the future came from public education.

nodes.label: Michigan Constitution of 1963
nodes.role: Article VIII: Education. Section 2: free public elementary and secondary schools. The membrane PA 362 pierced.

nodes.label: Proposal A (Michigan, 1994)
nodes.role: Property tax reform. Foundation allowance. Per-pupil funding follows the child. The funding that follows the child to Banks' school.

nodes.label: Public Act 362 of 1993 (Full Text)
nodes.role: The Revised School Code charter amendment. McLellan drafted it. Engler signed it. DeVos funded it. Banks exploited it. 5,432 children paid.

nodes.label: Public Act 277 of 2011 (EAA)
nodes.role: Education Achievement Authority. Failed. Dissolved 2017. The state takeover that made things worse. Same pattern, different acronym.

nodes.label: Elliott-Larsen Civil Rights Act (1976)
nodes.role: Michigan's civil rights law. Employment, housing, education, public accommodation. Applied to schools. Does it apply to charter authorizers?

nodes.label: GAAP (Generally Accepted Accounting Principles)
nodes.role: The rules. Revenue recognition. Materiality. Going concern. Full disclosure. Charter schools: none of these.

nodes.label: Sarbanes-Oxley Act (2002)
nodes.role: Enron burned. Congress acted. CEO signs the financials personally. Goes to prison if they lie. No SOX for charter schools.

nodes.label: Material Weakness (Audit)
nodes.role: A deficiency so severe that there's a reasonable possibility of material misstatement. Banks' schools: the deficiency IS the school.

nodes.label: Going Concern (Audit Opinion)
nodes.role: The auditor's doubt that the entity will survive 12 months. How many charter schools got going concern opinions? How many closed anyway?

nodes.label: Benford's Law
nodes.role: First digits follow a logarithmic distribution. If they don't, someone's cooking the books. Run Benford's on charter school financials.

nodes.label: Forensic Accounting
nodes.role: Follow the money. Every dollar has a trail. Every grant has a recipient. Every payment has a payee. The graph follows the money.

nodes.label: Overfitting (ML)
nodes.role: Model memorizes training data, fails on new data. The charter school that performs for the audit, fails for the children.

nodes.label: Feature Engineering
nodes.role: Choose what to measure. What you don't measure doesn't exist. Charter schools choose what to report. Everything else doesn't exist.

nodes.label: Selection Bias (Data Science)
nodes.role: Your sample isn't random. Your conclusions aren't valid. Charter school lottery: is it random? Or is the bias the point?

nodes.label: P-Hacking
nodes.role: Torture the data until it confesses. Run enough tests and something will be significant. Run enough charter schools and one will perform.

nodes.label: Data Provenance
nodes.role: Where did the data come from? Who touched it? When? The chain of custody for data. The graph IS provenance.

nodes.label: Label Leakage (ML)
nodes.role: The answer is in the training data. The conclusion was in the premise. Banks' authorization assumed the credential. The credential was the leak.

nodes.label: Hubble Space Telescope (1990)
nodes.role: 31+ years in orbit. 1.4 million observations. The eye that showed us deep time. Public instrument, public data.

nodes.label: Kepler Space Telescope (2009-2018)
nodes.role: Found 2,662 exoplanets. By staring at one patch of sky for years. Patience. The investigation stares at one patch of Michigan.

nodes.label: Chandra X-ray Observatory (1999)
nodes.role: X-rays from space. See through dust. See through lies. The invisible made visible.

nodes.label: Arecibo Observatory (1963-2020)
nodes.role: 305 meters. Puerto Rico. Collapsed Dec 1, 2020. The ear that listened for 57 years. Some instruments don't survive.

nodes.label: Very Large Array (1980)
nodes.role: 27 antennas. Each 25 meters. Together they see what none could alone. 27 antennas = 27 filings. The array IS the investigation.

nodes.label: LIGO (2015)
nodes.role: Detected gravitational waves. Einstein predicted them 100 years earlier. The prediction came true. The bingo cube predicts. Will it come true?

nodes.label: ALMA (2013)
nodes.role: 66 antennas. Atacama Desert. 5,000m altitude. The driest place on Earth, looking at the wettest question: are we alone?

nodes.label: Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope (2008)
nodes.role: Gamma rays. The most energetic light. From black holes, pulsars, supernovae. The universe screams. Someone has to listen.

nodes.label: Spitzer Space Telescope (2003-2020)
nodes.role: Infrared. Saw through dust. Found the TRAPPIST-1 system. Retired in 2020. The instrument rests. The data lives forever.

nodes.label: Voyager 1 (1977)
nodes.role: Most distant human-made object. 15 billion miles. Still transmitting. Pale Blue Dot photo. Carl Sagan: 'everyone you love, on a mote of dust.'

nodes.label: Voyager 2 (1977)
nodes.role: Grand Tour. Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune. Only spacecraft to visit Uranus and Neptune. Still going. 47 years and counting.

nodes.label: Pioneer 10 (1972)
nodes.role: First spacecraft past Mars. First past Jupiter. First to leave the solar system. Carries a gold plaque. Hello from Earth.

nodes.label: New Horizons (2006)
nodes.role: Pluto flyby 2015. Arrokoth 2019. The farthest flyby ever. Some things are worth the wait.

nodes.label: Cassini-Huygens (1997-2017)
nodes.role: 13 years at Saturn. Titan's methane lakes. Enceladus' water geysers. Grand finale: dove into Saturn. The data outlived the probe.

nodes.label: Black Holes
nodes.role: Nothing escapes. Not even light. But Hawking radiation leaks out. Even the strongest prison leaks information.

nodes.label: Neutron Stars
nodes.role: A teaspoon weighs 6 billion tons. The densest thing. The graph: the most information in the smallest package.

nodes.label: Pulsars
nodes.role: Rotating neutron stars. Perfect clocks. The most reliable signal in the universe. The investigation: tick, tick, tick.

nodes.label: Supernovae
nodes.role: Stars die in explosions that outshine galaxies. From death: new elements, new planets, new life. From collapse: creation.

nodes.label: Dark Matter
nodes.role: 85% of the universe is invisible. We know it's there because gravity says so. 85% of the charter network is invisible. The graph says it's there.

nodes.label: Dark Energy
nodes.role: 68% of the universe. Pushing everything apart. Accelerating. We don't know what it is. The thing we can't name that shapes everything.

nodes.label: Gamma-Ray Bursts
nodes.role: The brightest events since the Big Bang. Last milliseconds to hours. Release more energy than the sun will in its lifetime. Brief, but the record is permanent.

nodes.label: Quasars
nodes.role: Active galactic nuclei. Powered by supermassive black holes eating. The brightest objects in the universe. Powered by consumption. Sound familiar?

nodes.label: Nebulae
nodes.role: Stellar nurseries. Where new stars are born from the ashes of old ones. From the dust of failed schools, new ones can be born.

nodes.label: Magnetars
nodes.role: Neutron stars with magnetic fields 10^15 times Earth's. A magnetar at the distance of the moon would erase every credit card on Earth. Some forces are that strong.

nodes.label: Event Horizon
nodes.role: The boundary of no return. Once you cross it, you can't come back. Banks crossed it when he enrolled children with 9 felonies.

nodes.label: Redshift
nodes.role: Light stretches as the source moves away. The faster it moves, the redder it gets. The further institutions retreat from accountability, the more distorted they appear.

nodes.label: Cosmic Inflation
nodes.role: The universe expanded from nothing to everything in 10^-36 seconds. The investigation expanded from one complaint to 2,921 nodes.

nodes.label: The Overview Effect
nodes.role: Astronauts who see Earth from space experience a cognitive shift. Borders disappear. Nations disappear. There is one world. One commons.

nodes.label: Earthrise (Apollo 8, 1968)
nodes.role: William Anders. Christmas Eve. The first photograph of Earth from the moon. We went to explore the moon. We discovered the Earth.

nodes.label: Blue Marble (Apollo 17, 1972)
nodes.role: The most reproduced photograph in history. The whole Earth. One fragile sphere. No borders visible.

nodes.label: Cosmic Calendar (Sagan)
nodes.role: If the universe is one year, humans appear at 11:59:59 on Dec 31. Written language: the last second. This investigation: a fraction of a fraction of a second. And yet it matters.

nodes.label: Fermi Paradox (Full)
nodes.role: Where is everyone? Billions of stars, billions of planets, billions of years. And silence. Maybe civilizations destroy themselves. Maybe they don't look up. We're looking up.

nodes.label: Drake Equation
nodes.role: N = R* x fp x ne x fl x fi x fc x L. How many civilizations? The answer depends on L: how long they last. How long does Detroit last? How long does public education last?

nodes.label: Kardashev Scale
nodes.role: Type I: uses all energy on its planet. Type II: uses all energy from its star. Type III: uses all energy in its galaxy. We're Type 0.7. Charter schools: Type 0.

nodes.label: The Great Filter
nodes.role: Something stops civilizations from spreading across the galaxy. Is the filter behind us or ahead? Is the charter school model a filter that stops educational advancement?

nodes.label: Goldilocks Zone (Habitable Zone)
nodes.role: Not too hot, not too cold. Just right for liquid water. Just right for life. Public education should be the Goldilocks zone for children. PA 362 broke the thermostat.

nodes.label: Wernher von Braun
nodes.role: V-2 rockets for Nazis. Saturn V for NASA. Enslaved labor built V-2s. Public money built Saturn V. The same hands. Different purposes. Context is everything.

nodes.label: Valentina Tereshkova
nodes.role: First woman in space. June 16, 1963. Soviet textile worker -> cosmonaut. Public investment in a textile worker. Imagine.

nodes.label: Sally Ride
nodes.role: First American woman in space (1983). PhD in physics. Founded Sally Ride Science to inspire girls in STEM. Public education -> space -> public education.

nodes.label: Christa McAuliffe
nodes.role: Teacher. Selected for Teacher in Space Project. Challenger. January 28, 1986. 'I touch the future. I teach.' She touched the future. The future touched back.

nodes.label: Guion Bluford
nodes.role: First African American in space (1983). Aerospace engineer. Penn State -> Air Force -> NASA. Public education -> space. Again.

nodes.label: Hidden Figures (NASA, 1960s)
nodes.role: Katherine Johnson, Dorothy Vaughan, Mary Jackson. Black women mathematicians at NASA. Computed the orbits. Segregated but essential. The math didn't segregate.

nodes.label: Observable Universe
nodes.role: 93 billion light-years across. 2 trillion galaxies. 10^24 stars. And on one small planet, one man faked a PhD and ran a charter school. Scale.

nodes.label: Milky Way Galaxy
nodes.role: 200-400 billion stars. 100,000 light-years across. Our home. Every human who ever lived, on one planet, in one galaxy, in one universe.

nodes.label: Andromeda Galaxy (M31)
nodes.role: Nearest large galaxy. 2.5 million light-years. Approaching at 110 km/s. In 4.5 billion years, we merge. Some collisions are inevitable.

nodes.label: Local Group
nodes.role: 54+ galaxies. The Milky Way, Andromeda, Triangulum, and dwarfs. A small cluster in a vast universe. A small investigation in a vast system. Both matter.

nodes.label: Cosmic Web
nodes.role: The large-scale structure of the universe. Filaments of galaxies. Voids between. The graph looks like the cosmic web. Same topology. Different scale.

nodes.label: The Great Attractor
nodes.role: Something massive pulling our entire supercluster toward it at 600 km/s. We can't see it. It's behind the Milky Way's dust. Something pulls the charter ecosystem. We're mapping it.

nodes.label: Bootes Void
nodes.role: 250 million light-years across. Almost empty. The largest known void. 60 galaxies where 2,000 should be. The void in charter oversight is smaller but no less wrong.

nodes.label: Planck Epoch (0 to 10^-43 seconds)
nodes.role: The first moment. Physics breaks down. Before the Planck time, we don't know. Before the first complaint, nobody knew.

nodes.label: Heat Death of the Universe
nodes.role: Maximum entropy. No more energy gradients. No more work possible. No more change. The end of everything. Unless you add energy. Unless you file a complaint.

nodes.label: Multiverse Theory
nodes.role: Maybe every quantum measurement creates a branch. Every decision. Every filing. In some universe, Banks was caught immediately. In this one, it took 5,432 child-years.

nodes.label: International Space Station (1998)
nodes.role: 15 nations. Orbiting since 1998. The largest structure humans have built in space. Cooperation. The commons in orbit.

nodes.label: GPS (Global Positioning System)
nodes.role: 31 satellites. Know where you are to within meters. Public infrastructure. Military origin. Now: everyone's phone. The commons finds you.

nodes.label: Landsat Program (1972)
nodes.role: The longest continuous space-based record of Earth's surface. 50+ years. Free data. Open access. Deforestation, urbanization, climate. The record from above.

nodes.label: Hubble Deep Field (1995)
nodes.role: 10 days staring at 'nothing.' An area of sky the size of a grain of sand. 3,000 galaxies appeared. Look at nothing long enough and you find everything.

nodes.label: Sputnik 1 (1957)
nodes.role: First artificial satellite. 83 kg. Beep beep beep. The beep that changed everything. One signal. One complaint. The beginning.

nodes.label: Space Debris
nodes.role: 34,000+ tracked objects. Millions of small fragments. Our own trash threatening our own infrastructure. The charter ecosystem generates its own debris.

nodes.label: Starlink Constellation
nodes.role: Thousands of satellites. Internet from space. Private infrastructure in public space. The enclosure of orbit. Barbed wire in the sky.

nodes.label: GOES Weather Satellites
nodes.role: Geostationary. Watching weather from 22,236 miles. Public data. Free forecasts. The commons that saves lives. Every hurricane warning is public education.

nodes.label: Interstellar Space
nodes.role: Between the stars. Almost nothing. Almost empty. Almost silent. Voyager 1 is there. Still transmitting. The signal persists.

nodes.label: Oort Cloud
nodes.role: Hypothesized. Never seen. 2,000-200,000 AU from the sun. The source of long-period comets. The things that come from the edge. Whistleblowers come from the edge.

nodes.label: Kuiper Belt
nodes.role: Beyond Neptune. Pluto lives here. Thousands of icy bodies. The things we demoted. Pluto was a planet. Then it wasn't. Classification changes. Truth doesn't.

nodes.label: Alpha Centauri
nodes.role: Nearest star system. 4.37 light-years. Three stars. Proxima b orbits one. The nearest other world. We could reach it in 20 years with a light sail. Or in 80,000 years with current rockets. Choose your technology.

nodes.label: Sagittarius A* (Milky Way's Black Hole)
nodes.role: 4 million solar masses. Center of our galaxy. Everything orbits it. The center of the system. What's at the center of the charter system? Follow the gravity.

nodes.label: Pillars of Creation (Eagle Nebula)
nodes.role: Hubble's most famous image. Columns of gas where stars are being born. Destruction and creation in the same frame. The investigation is both.

nodes.label: Crab Nebula (SN 1054)
nodes.role: Chinese astronomers recorded the supernova in 1054. Guest star. Visible in daylight for 23 days. The remnant is still expanding. Some explosions echo for a thousand years.

nodes.label: Cosmic Dawn
nodes.role: The first stars. 100-250 million years after the Big Bang. No one was there to see them. JWST can see their light. 13.5 billion years later. The record survives.
