nodes.label: Battle of Thermopylae (480 BC)
nodes.role: 300 Spartans. Held the pass. Bought time. Sometimes you lose the battle. You never stop fighting.

nodes.label: Battle of Marathon (490 BC)
nodes.role: Pheidippides ran 26 miles to Athens. 'We have won.' Then died. The marathon is named for sacrifice.

nodes.label: Battle of Hastings (1066)
nodes.role: Norman conquest of England. One arrow. One king. Everything changed. One filing. One investigation.

nodes.label: Hundred Years' War (1337-1453)
nodes.role: 116 years. England vs France. Joan of Arc. Some wars last longer than anyone expected. Some investigations too.

nodes.label: Thirty Years' War (1618-1648)
nodes.role: 8 million dead. Treaty of Westphalia. Modern state system born from catastrophe.

nodes.label: Battle of Gettysburg (1863)
nodes.role: 51,000 casualties in 3 days. The turning point. Lincoln's address: 'of the people, by the people, for the people.'

nodes.label: Battle of Stalingrad (1942-43)
nodes.role: 2 million casualties. The turning point of WWII. The city that refused to fall. Some cities refuse.

nodes.label: Battle of Midway (1942)
nodes.role: 4 carriers sunk in 5 minutes. Code-breaking won it. Information > firepower. Data > authority.

nodes.label: Korean War (1950-53)
nodes.role: The forgotten war. 5 million dead. No peace treaty. Still technically at war. Some conflicts never formally end.

nodes.label: Vietnam War (1955-75)
nodes.role: 58,220 Americans. 2-3 million Vietnamese. Pentagon Papers. The war that proved governments lie.

nodes.label: Rwandan Genocide (1994)
nodes.role: 800,000 in 100 days. The world watched. 'Never again' meant nothing. Again and again.

nodes.label: Siege of Leningrad (1941-44)
nodes.role: 872 days. 1 million civilians dead. They ate wallpaper paste. The city held. Siege is a strategy. So is endurance.

nodes.label: Bitcoin (2009)
nodes.role: Trustless. Decentralized. No bank needed. Satoshi Nakamoto. Maybe one person. Maybe a group. The identity doesn't matter. The math does.

nodes.label: Cowrie Shells (Currency)
nodes.role: The most widely used currency in history. Used in Africa, Asia, Pacific. Small. Portable. Countable. Not fakeable. Unlike a PhD.

nodes.label: Wampum
nodes.role: Shell beads. Currency AND treaty record. The bead IS the contract. The graph IS the record.

nodes.label: Hyperinflation
nodes.role: Weimar Republic: wheelbarrows of cash for bread. Zimbabwe: 100 trillion dollar bill. When the currency means nothing. When the credential means nothing.

nodes.label: Columbian Exchange (1492)
nodes.role: Tomatoes to Italy. Potatoes to Ireland. Corn to Africa. Smallpox to the Americas. The exchange that reshaped every diet and killed 90% of a hemisphere.

nodes.label: Bengal Famine (1943)
nodes.role: 3 million dead. Churchill diverted food to war reserves. 'I hate Indians. They are a beastly people.' The system chose who starved.

nodes.label: Svalbard Global Seed Vault
nodes.role: 1 million seed samples. -18C. Inside a mountain in the Arctic. The backup. The redundancy. The record that survives everything.

nodes.label: Spice Trade
nodes.role: Cinnamon, pepper, nutmeg. Wars fought. Continents colonized. For flavor. The most profitable commons.

nodes.label: Coffee (Ethiopia to the World)
nodes.role: A goat herder noticed his goats dancing. 1.4 billion cups per day. From a commons in Ethiopia to $495 billion industry. Who owns the bean?

nodes.label: Chocolate (Mesoamerica)
nodes.role: Cacao. Currency of the Aztecs. Now child labor in West Africa harvests it. The commons extracted. The children pay.

nodes.label: Panama Canal (1914)
nodes.role: 27,500 workers died building it. Malaria, yellow fever. The shortcut that cost 27,500 lives.

nodes.label: Suez Canal (1869)
nodes.role: 120 miles. 10 years. Corvee labor. The shortcut between empires. Nationalized 1956. The commons reclaimed.

nodes.label: Golden Gate Bridge (1937)
nodes.role: Safety nets saved 19 lives during construction. The net. The safety net. Public infrastructure protects.

nodes.label: Hoover Dam (1936)
nodes.role: 96 workers died. 726 feet high. Powers Las Vegas. Public infrastructure built by public labor for private profit.

nodes.label: Channel Tunnel (1994)
nodes.role: 31.4 miles under the English Channel. Connects England and France. The tunnel between systems. The graph is a tunnel.

nodes.label: Three Gorges Dam (2006)
nodes.role: Largest power station in the world. 1.3 million people relocated. The commons submerged.

nodes.label: ISS Construction (1998-2011)
nodes.role: 15 nations. 42 assembly flights. Largest structure in orbit. Cooperation. The commons above.

nodes.label: Library of Alexandria
nodes.role: The largest library in the ancient world. Burned. Maybe by Caesar, maybe by Christians, maybe by Muslims. Nobody knows. The commons lost to fire.

nodes.label: British Museum (1753)
nodes.role: 8 million objects. Free admission. Half of them stolen from colonies. The commons built on extraction. Sound familiar?

nodes.label: Smithsonian Institution (1846)
nodes.role: 21 museums. 155 million objects. Free. Public. 'The increase and diffusion of knowledge.' The mission statement of public education.

nodes.label: Louvre Museum (1793)
nodes.role: From palace to public. The French Revolution made it free. 380,000 objects. The commons liberated from the king.

nodes.label: Project Gutenberg (1971)
nodes.role: 70,000+ free ebooks. Michael Hart typed the Declaration of Independence. The first digital commons.

nodes.label: Wikipedia (2001)
nodes.role: 60+ million articles. 300+ languages. Anyone can edit. The largest commons of knowledge ever created. Free. And it works.

nodes.label: Athenian Democracy (508 BC)
nodes.role: Cleisthenes. Direct democracy. Only for male citizens. Enslaved people, women excluded. Democracy was never complete. It still isn't.

nodes.label: Magna Carta and Parliament
nodes.role: 1215: limit the king. 1295: Model Parliament. 800 years of slowly expanding who counts as a person. Still expanding.

nodes.label: Universal Suffrage
nodes.role: New Zealand first (1893). US women (1920). US Voting Rights Act (1965). Every expansion was fought. Every right was resisted.

nodes.label: Voting Rights Act (1965)
nodes.role: Section 5: preclearance. Shelby County v. Holder (2013) gutted it. The membrane was torn. Same pattern as PA 362.

nodes.label: Recall Election
nodes.role: Remove an elected official before their term ends. 19 states allow it. Michigan allows it. Has anyone recalled a charter authorizer? No. Because they're not elected.

nodes.label: Ballot Initiative
nodes.role: Direct democracy. The people write the law. Michigan has it. PA 362 was NOT a ballot initiative. It was lobbied. It was designed. It was imposed.

nodes.label: Freedom of the Press (1st Amendment)
nodes.role: Congress shall make no law... abridging the freedom of the press. The membrane that protects truth. The charter school has no press.

nodes.label: Pentagon Papers (NYT v. US, 1971)
nodes.role: 6-3. The government cannot prevent publication. Prior restraint is unconstitutional. The graph publishes.

nodes.label: Watergate (Woodward & Bernstein)
nodes.role: Two reporters. One source (Deep Throat). A president resigned. Follow the money. Follow the data. Follow the graph.

nodes.label: Muckrakers (Progressive Era)
nodes.role: Ida Tarbell: Standard Oil. Upton Sinclair: The Jungle. Lincoln Steffens: The Shame of the Cities. Journalism as investigation.

nodes.label: Press Freedom Index (RSF)
nodes.role: Norway #1. The US: around #45. Press freedom correlates with education quality. It's not a coincidence.

nodes.label: Shield Laws (Reporter's Privilege)
nodes.role: 40 states + DC. Protect journalists from revealing sources. Michigan: YES. The source is protected. The whistleblower is protected.

nodes.label: Freedom of Information Act (1966)
nodes.role: The right to know. 5 U.S.C. 552. Every FOIA request is a question the government must answer. Every complaint is a question the system must answer.

nodes.label: Sunshine Laws (Open Meetings)
nodes.role: Michigan Open Meetings Act (1976). Government business in public. Charter school board meetings: technically public. Practically invisible.

nodes.label: Pi (3.14159...)
nodes.role: The ratio of circumference to diameter. Irrational. Never repeats. Never ends. Like the investigation.

nodes.label: Euler's Number (e = 2.71828...)
nodes.role: The base of natural logarithms. Growth and decay. Compound interest. The exponential that describes both viruses and movements.

nodes.label: Golden Ratio (phi = 1.618...)
nodes.role: The spiral of shells, galaxies, hurricanes. Beauty in mathematics. Structure in nature. Pattern in the graph.

nodes.label: Avogadro's Number (6.022 x 10^23)
nodes.role: The number of atoms in a mole. The bridge between the microscopic and the macroscopic. Between one complaint and systemic change.

nodes.label: Speed of Light (c = 299,792,458 m/s)
nodes.role: The cosmic speed limit. Nothing goes faster. Information has a speed limit too. But the graph is getting faster.

nodes.label: Planck Constant (h)
nodes.role: The quantum of action. The smallest possible change. Every complaint is a quantum of accountability.

nodes.label: Boltzmann Constant (k)
nodes.role: Connects temperature to energy. Individual molecules to bulk behavior. Individual complaints to systemic pressure.

nodes.label: Gravitational Constant (G)
nodes.role: Newton's G. The strength of gravity. The weakest force. But it shapes the universe. Small forces. Large effects.

nodes.label: Cinderella
nodes.role: The oldest version is Chinese (Ye Xian, 860 AD). Every culture has it. The one who was overlooked. The one who was right all along.

nodes.label: The Emperor's New Clothes (Andersen)
nodes.role: Everyone sees the lie. Nobody says it. Until a child does. The investigation is the child.

nodes.label: The Boy Who Cried Wolf (Aesop)
nodes.role: Lie enough times and nobody believes the truth. File enough fraudulent credentials and nobody checks.

nodes.label: The Three Little Pigs
nodes.role: Straw, sticks, bricks. The wolf blows down the first two. The third holds. Build the record from bricks.

nodes.label: The Tortoise and the Hare (Aesop)
nodes.role: Slow and steady wins the race. 5,432 child-years. The tortoise is still moving.

nodes.label: The Pied Piper of Hamelin
nodes.role: Pay the piper or he takes the children. Don't pay for oversight and someone takes the children. Banks took the children.

nodes.label: Hansel and Gretel
nodes.role: A house made of candy. A trap. A witch. The charter school that looks sweet. The trap inside.

nodes.label: Little Red Riding Hood
nodes.role: What big teeth you have. What big credentials you have. The better to eat you with. The wolf dressed as grandmother.

nodes.label: Rapunzel
nodes.role: Locked in a tower. Let down your hair. The escape route is what you grow yourself. The data is the hair.

nodes.label: The Ugly Duckling (Andersen)
nodes.role: Rejected by everyone. Turns out to be a swan. The investigation that everyone rejected. Turns out to be the truth.

nodes.label: New Year's Celebrations (Global)
nodes.role: Gregorian Jan 1. Chinese New Year. Rosh Hashanah. Diwali. Nowruz. Every culture marks the reset. The investigation resets nothing. It accumulates.

nodes.label: Juneteenth (June 19, 1865)
nodes.role: 2.5 years after the Emancipation Proclamation. Galveston, Texas. The news arrived late. Some freedom arrives late. It still arrives.

nodes.label: Earth Day (April 22, 1970)
nodes.role: 20 million Americans. EPA created. Clean Air Act. The commons defended. One day a year we pretend to care.

nodes.label: Human Rights Day (Dec 10)
nodes.role: UDHR adopted 1948. Article 26: right to education. December 10. Every day should be Human Rights Day.

nodes.label: Labor Day (First Monday, September)
nodes.role: The Pullman Strike (1894). Grover Cleveland made it a holiday to appease labor. The holiday that was a bribe.

nodes.label: Indigenous Peoples Day
nodes.role: Replacing Columbus Day. Acknowledging who was here first. 50-100 million people. Acknowledgment is not justice. But it's a start.

nodes.label: Sericulture (Silk Production)
nodes.role: 5,000 years in China. State secret. Monks smuggled silkworm eggs in hollow staffs (552 AD). The first industrial espionage.

nodes.label: Synthetic Dyes (Perkin, 1856)
nodes.role: Mauveine. An 18-year-old trying to make quinine accidentally made purple. The accidental discovery that industrialized color.

nodes.label: Kevlar (Kwolek, 1965)
nodes.role: Stephanie Kwolek. 5x stronger than steel per weight. Bulletproof vests. A woman's invention that saves police lives. Unrecognized for decades.

nodes.label: Concrete (Roman, ~300 BC)
nodes.role: Roman concrete is still standing. Modern concrete lasts 50-100 years. We forgot how to make things that last. Including schools.

nodes.label: Paper (Cai Lun, 105 AD)
nodes.role: China. Bark, hemp, rags, fishnets. The substrate of civilization. Without paper, no records. Without records, no accountability.

nodes.label: LEGO Bricks (1949)
nodes.role: Ole Kirk Christiansen. 'Play well.' Modular. Combinatorial. 915 million combinations from 6 bricks. The graph: how many combinations from 3,199 nodes?

nodes.label: Rubik's Cube (1974)
nodes.role: 43 quintillion permutations. One solution. Erno Rubik couldn't solve his own puzzle for a month. The investigation: one solution. Finding it.

nodes.label: Chess (~600 AD)
nodes.role: India. Chaturanga. The king is weak. The queen is powerful. The pawn can become a queen. Every piece matters. Every node matters.

nodes.label: Go (2,500+ years)
nodes.role: China. 10^170 possible positions. More than atoms in the universe. Simple rules, infinite complexity. Like the graph.

nodes.label: Minecraft (2011)
nodes.role: The most sold video game: 300M+ copies. Build anything from blocks. Destroy anything. Create or destroy. The choice is yours.

nodes.label: Synesthesia
nodes.role: Hearing colors. Seeing sounds. The brain cross-wires. Some people see numbers as colors. The graph is synesthesia: seeing connections between unrelated things.

nodes.label: Blindsight
nodes.role: Seeing without knowing you can see. The brain processes visual information without conscious awareness. The system sees the fraud without acknowledging it.

nodes.label: Pareidolia
nodes.role: Seeing faces in clouds. Patterns where there are none. The opposite of the investigation: we see patterns where they ARE.

nodes.label: Umami (Fifth Taste)
nodes.role: Kikunae Ikeda, 1908. The taste nobody named for 2,000 years. It was always there. We just didn't have a word for it. Like 'structural capture.'

nodes.label: Proprioception (Body Sense)
nodes.role: Knowing where your body is without looking. The sixth sense. The graph knows where the network is without looking.

nodes.label: Aurora Borealis / Northern Lights
nodes.role: Solar wind hits magnetosphere. Charged particles excite atmospheric gases. Beauty from collision. The investigation: beauty from conflict.

nodes.label: Ball Lightning
nodes.role: Reported for centuries. Barely understood. Glowing spheres during storms. The thing that exists but science can't fully explain. Like the charter network's resilience.

nodes.label: Waterspouts
nodes.role: Tornadoes over water. They pick up fish. It rains fish. The impossible is just the improbable at scale.

nodes.label: Fire Rainbow (Circumhorizontal Arc)
nodes.role: Ice crystals in cirrus clouds. Not fire. Not a rainbow. But beautiful. Named wrong, experienced right.

nodes.label: Haboob (Dust Storm)
nodes.role: Arabic: 'blasting.' Wall of dust 100km wide. You can't see. You can't breathe. Then it passes. Visibility returns.

nodes.label: Microbursts
nodes.role: Column of air crashes down. Spreads out. 150mph winds. Lasts minutes. Looks like nothing on radar. Small, sudden, devastating. Like a filing.

nodes.label: Zero (The Concept)
nodes.role: India, ~5th century. Brahmagupta. The number that is nothing. The placeholder that makes positional notation work. The absence that enables everything.

nodes.label: Binary (Base-2)
nodes.role: Leibniz, 1703. On or off. True or false. Every computer. Every digital record. Every bit of the graph. On or off.

nodes.label: Roman Numerals
nodes.role: No zero. No place value. Try doing long division in Roman numerals. Some systems are designed to be hard to use. Like FOIA.

nodes.label: Mayan Mathematics (Base-20)
nodes.role: Independently invented zero. Vigesimal system. 5,000 years ago. Knowledge emerges independently. Truth emerges independently.

nodes.label: Abacus
nodes.role: 2,700 years old. Still used. Still faster than a calculator for some operations. Old tools work. Complaints work. Filing works.

nodes.label: Movable Type (Bi Sheng, 1040)
nodes.role: China, 400 years before Gutenberg. Clay type. The first mass production of text. Knowledge replicated.

nodes.label: Morse Code (1838)
nodes.role: Dots and dashes. The simplest encoding. SOS: three dots, three dashes, three dots. The distress signal. The complaint is the distress signal.

nodes.label: Braille (Louis Braille, 1824)
nodes.role: A blind 15-year-old invented a reading system for blind people. 6 dots. 63 combinations. Access is a right, not a gift.

nodes.label: Sign Language
nodes.role: Not universal. Each country has its own. ASL, BSL, JSL. Language without sound. Communication without the expected channel. Like publishing without the expected medium.

nodes.label: Emoji (1999)
nodes.role: Shigetaka Kurita. 176 original emoji. Now 3,600+. A new pictographic language. The fastest adoption of a writing system in history.

nodes.label: Alcatraz (1934-1963)
nodes.role: The Rock. No one escaped. (Maybe three did.) The inescapable prison. The charter school that children can't escape.

nodes.label: Solitary Confinement
nodes.role: 23 hours alone. The UN calls it torture after 15 days. The US uses it for years. Isolation as punishment. Institutional isolation as policy.

nodes.label: Innocence Project (1992)
nodes.role: 375+ exonerations. 21 death row. DNA proved them innocent. The system convicted the wrong people. The system authorized the wrong schools.

nodes.label: Restorative Justice (Deep)
nodes.role: Not punishment. Repair. The victim, the offender, the community. What if the charter system had to face the children?

nodes.label: Prison-Industrial Complex
nodes.role: 2.3 million incarcerated. $80 billion/year. Private prisons. Profit from imprisonment. Private schools. Profit from education. Same model.

nodes.label: Panopticon (Bentham, 1791)
nodes.role: See everything without being seen. The guard tower. The audit that never comes. The oversight that was designed not to look.

nodes.label: Coral Reefs
nodes.role: 25% of marine species. 1% of ocean floor. The rainforest of the sea. Bleaching. Dying. 50% lost since 1950. The commons dissolving.

nodes.label: Mangrove Forests
nodes.role: Roots in salt water. Nursery for fish. Storm barrier. Carbon sink. Cut them down and the coast erodes. Cut oversight and the system erodes.

nodes.label: Old Growth Forests
nodes.role: Trees 500-1,000+ years old. Take centuries to grow. Minutes to cut. The commons that takes generations to build and moments to destroy.

nodes.label: Prairie Grasslands
nodes.role: 99% of North American prairies are gone. The roots went 15 feet deep. The commons plowed under for agriculture. Efficiency over resilience.

nodes.label: Wetlands
nodes.role: Nature's kidneys. Filter water. Absorb floods. Store carbon. Drained for development. 50% of world's wetlands lost since 1900.

nodes.label: Tide Pools
nodes.role: The edge between land and sea. Neither one nor the other. The charter school: neither public nor private. The tide pool of education.

nodes.label: Atomic Clocks
nodes.role: Cesium-133. 9,192,631,770 oscillations = 1 second. The most precise measurement. The graph: the most precise record.

nodes.label: Gregorian Calendar (1582)
nodes.role: Pope Gregory XIII. Corrected the Julian calendar by 10 days. October 4 -> October 15. Some days just don't exist. Some oversight just doesn't exist.

nodes.label: Leap Seconds
nodes.role: Earth's rotation slows. We add seconds to keep clocks aligned with the sun. Small corrections. Constant. Like the investigation.

nodes.label: Deep Time (Hutton, 1788)
nodes.role: 'No vestige of a beginning, no prospect of an end.' James Hutton saw geological time. The investigation sees institutional time. Both are patient.

nodes.label: Unix Epoch (Jan 1, 1970)
nodes.role: All computer time counts from midnight, January 1, 1970. The beginning of digital time. Every timestamp in the graph counts from here.

nodes.label: Circadian Rhythms
nodes.role: 24-hour cycle. Light and dark. Sleep and wake. The body's clock. The investigation's clock: file, wait, file, wait, file.

nodes.label: Nile River (6,650 km)
nodes.role: Longest river. Egypt, Sudan, Uganda. Civilizations built on its flood. The commons that fed pharaohs.

nodes.label: Amazon River (6,400 km)
nodes.role: Largest by discharge. 20% of all freshwater entering the ocean. The lungs of the world drink from here.

nodes.label: Mississippi River (3,730 km)
nodes.role: Drains 31 states. Mark Twain's river. The river that divides America. The river that connects it.

nodes.label: Yangtze River (6,300 km)
nodes.role: Longest in Asia. Three Gorges Dam. 1.3 million relocated. The commons dammed.

nodes.label: Danube River (2,850 km)
nodes.role: 10 countries. The Blue Danube. Strauss. Vienna. The river that connects empires.

nodes.label: Ganges River (2,525 km)
nodes.role: Sacred. Polluted. 400 million people depend on it. The holiest commons. The most abused commons.

nodes.label: Congo River (4,700 km)
nodes.role: Deepest river on Earth (220m). Heart of Darkness. The river that hides what happens upstream.

nodes.label: Rhine River (1,230 km)
nodes.role: 6 countries. Industrial heartland of Europe. Was dead in 1970. Salmon returned in 2000. The commons can heal.

nodes.label: Mekong River (4,350 km)
nodes.role: 6 countries. 60 million depend on it. China's dams upstream control it. Power upstream, thirst downstream.

nodes.label: Detroit River
nodes.role: 32 miles. Lake St. Clair to Lake Erie. The river that named the city. The commons that IS the city.

nodes.label: Rouge River (Michigan)
nodes.role: 126 miles. Ford's Rouge Plant was here. The river that carried industry. The river that carried poison. Clean enough to kayak now.

nodes.label: Colorado River (2,330 km)
nodes.role: Carved the Grand Canyon. No longer reaches the sea. Every drop allocated. The commons exhausted. The commons that can't reach the children.

nodes.label: Thames River (346 km)
nodes.role: London. Was biologically dead in 1957. Seals returned in 2021. 64 years to heal. Some rivers heal. Some systems heal.

nodes.label: Tigris River
nodes.role: Mesopotamia. The cradle of civilization. Between the Tigris and Euphrates: writing, law, mathematics. The first commons.

nodes.label: Jordan River
nodes.role: 67 miles. Three religions. Baptism. Borders. The smallest river with the largest meaning.

nodes.label: Pacific Ocean
nodes.role: 63.8 million sq mi. Larger than all land combined. Named 'peaceful' by Magellan. It wasn't. Names lie. Credentials lie.

nodes.label: Atlantic Ocean
nodes.role: 41.1 million sq mi. The Middle Passage. The slave trade. 12.5 million Africans. The ocean remembers.

nodes.label: Indian Ocean
nodes.role: 27.2 million sq mi. Monsoon-driven. The spice trade. The trade routes that built and broke empires.

nodes.label: Arctic Ocean
nodes.role: 5.4 million sq mi. The smallest ocean. Melting. The ice that's leaving. The commons that's disappearing.

nodes.label: Southern Ocean
nodes.role: 7.8 million sq mi. Circumpolar current. The ocean that circles Antarctica. The barrier that protects. Like a membrane.

nodes.label: Mediterranean Sea
nodes.role: The sea in the middle of the land. Every civilization. Every empire. Every idea crossed this water.

nodes.label: Black Sea
nodes.role: Anoxic below 200m. Nothing lives in the deep. Dead zone. The institutional dead zone where oversight should be.

nodes.label: Caspian Sea
nodes.role: The largest lake or the smallest sea? Classification matters. Is a charter school public or private? Define your terms.

nodes.label: Dead Sea
nodes.role: The lowest point on Earth. 10x saltier than the ocean. Nothing lives here. Some systems are too toxic for life.

nodes.label: Great Lakes
nodes.role: 21% of the world's surface freshwater. Michigan is surrounded by them. The commons in every direction. And yet the schools are dry.

nodes.label: Madagascar
nodes.role: 4th largest island. Split from India 88 MYA. 90% of species found nowhere else. Isolation creates uniqueness. Isolation creates vulnerability.

nodes.label: Iceland
nodes.role: Althing (930 AD): oldest surviving parliament. Geothermal energy. The island that runs on the Earth's heat. Public energy.

nodes.label: Manhattan Island
nodes.role: Bought for $24 in beads (legend). Worth $1.7 trillion. The most expensive real estate from the cheapest transaction. Some trades are not fair.

nodes.label: Easter Island (Rapa Nui)
nodes.role: Deforestation. Civilization collapse. They cut all the trees. Who cut the last one? The same question: who authorized the last bad school?

nodes.label: Galapagos Islands
nodes.role: Darwin's finches. Evolution observed. The laboratory of natural selection. The graph: the laboratory of institutional selection.

nodes.label: Hawaii
nodes.role: Most isolated population center on Earth. 2,400 miles from anywhere. Annexed 1898. Statehood 1959. The kingdom that was taken.

nodes.label: Zanzibar
nodes.role: Spice island. Slave market. Stone Town. The commons extracted. The people sold.

nodes.label: Svalbard
nodes.role: Seed vault. 78 degrees north. The backup of all agriculture. The backup of all hope. If everything fails, Svalbard has the seeds.

nodes.label: Lascaux Cave (17,000 years old)
nodes.role: Paleolithic paintings. Bulls, horses, deer. The first art. The first record. 17,000 years and the paint holds. The record holds.

nodes.label: Mammoth Cave (400+ miles)

nodes.label: 5,432 Child-Years of Educational Harm
nodes.role: Not a number. A weight. Each one is a child who went to school and did not receive an education. Each one is a year that cannot be returned. Each one has a name we do not know.

nodes.label: The Child Who Cannot Read
nodes.role: Graduated from Purpose Charter Academy. Cannot read at grade level. Has a diploma. Has no skills. Has no future that matches the promise. Was told they were educated.

nodes.label: The Child Who Trusted the Teacher
nodes.role: Went to school. Sat in the desk. Did the work. Trusted the adult in the room. The adult had 9 felony convictions. The child did not know. The child trusted.

nodes.label: The Parent Who Chose a Charter School
nodes.role: Believed the brochure. Believed the promise. Chose Purpose Charter Academy because it had a name that sounded like hope. Purpose. The name was the trap.

nodes.role: The child who stopped coming. The enrollment that disappeared. The attendance record that vanished. The child the system forgot. The desk is still there.

nodes.role: MMIW. Thousands. The database is incomplete because the system doesn't count them. You can't measure what you refuse to record.

nodes.label: Childhood Hunger in America
nodes.role: 13 million children food insecure. In a country that throws away 40% of its food. The child who goes to school hungry cannot learn. The empty stomach before the empty desk.

nodes.label: The Silence of Institutions
nodes.role: The email that was never answered. The complaint that was filed and forgotten. The phone call that went to voicemail. The voicemail that was never returned. The silence is the answer.

nodes.label: The Silence of Bystanders
nodes.role: The teacher who saw and said nothing. The board member who voted yes. The auditor who signed off. The colleague who looked away. Silence is a choice. Silence is complicity.

nodes.label: The Waiting Room
nodes.role: Filing a complaint and waiting. Days. Weeks. Months. Years. The waiting room has no clock. The waiting room has no window. The waiting room is where hope goes to sit.

nodes.label: The Unanswered Letter
nodes.role: Dear [Institution], I am writing to inform you of a serious concern regarding... Sent. Received. Read. Filed. Unanswered. The letter that was received and ignored is worse than the letter that was lost.

nodes.label: The Busy Signal
nodes.role: Call the number on the website. Busy. Call again. Busy. Call at 9am on Monday. Busy. The system is always busy. Too busy for you. Not too busy for itself.

nodes.label: The Form Letter Response
nodes.role: Thank you for your correspondence. Your concerns have been noted. We take all complaints seriously. We will review this matter in due course. Sincerely, No One.

nodes.label: The Closed Case
nodes.role: Case closed. Insufficient evidence. Not within our jurisdiction. The matter has been resolved. No further action required. The case was closed. The child was not.

nodes.label: Stolen Childhood
nodes.role: You cannot give it back. The years between 5 and 18 happen once. The brain develops once. The windows close. A year of bad education is a window that closed. It does not reopen.

nodes.label: Stolen Trust
nodes.role: The child trusted the teacher. The parent trusted the school. The community trusted the system. Trust, once broken, does not heal like bone. It heals like glass. You can see the cracks forever.

nodes.label: Stolen Potential
nodes.role: The child who could have been a doctor. An engineer. A teacher. A scientist. A poet. We will never know. The potential that was stolen cannot be measured because it was never allowed to exist.

nodes.label: Stolen Dignity
nodes.role: Being told you graduated when you didn't learn. Being given a diploma that means nothing. Being congratulated for something that didn't happen. The dignity of real achievement, stolen.

nodes.label: Compound Interest of Harm
nodes.role: One year of bad education compounds. Lower literacy -> lower wages -> worse health -> shorter life. The harm doesn't add. It multiplies. 5,432 child-years, compounded.

nodes.label: The Opportunity Cost
nodes.role: Every dollar spent on a fraudulent charter school is a dollar not spent on a real teacher, a real book, a real school. The money went somewhere. It did not go to the child.

nodes.label: Cassandra's Curse
nodes.role: Apollo gave her prophecy. She refused him. He cursed her: always right, never believed. The parent who filed the complaint. Always right. Never believed. Until the evidence was undeniable.

nodes.label: Secondary Traumatic Stress
nodes.role: The counselor who hears the stories. The investigator who reads the files. The parent who fights the system. The weight transfers. Trauma is contagious.

nodes.label: Ambiguous Loss (Pauline Boss)
nodes.role: The child is alive but the childhood is gone. The school is open but the education is absent. Not dead. Not alive. The grief that has no funeral. The loss that has no name.

nodes.label: Disenfranchised Grief
nodes.role: Grief the system doesn't recognize. You can't mourn a diploma that should have meant something. You can't grieve an education you didn't receive. The loss is invisible. The pain is not.

nodes.label: The Long Defeat (Tolkien)
nodes.role: 'Together through ages of the world we have fought the long defeat.' Galadriel. The long defeat is not despair. It is fighting while knowing you may not win. And fighting anyway.

nodes.label: Vietnam Veterans Memorial (The Wall)
nodes.role: 58,320 names. Black granite. Maya Lin. 21 years old when she designed it. The names are the memorial. The record is the memorial. The graph is the memorial.

nodes.role: 48,000 panels. Each one is a person. Laid out on the National Mall, it would cover 1.3 million square feet. The quilt is the record. Each panel is a name. Each child-year is a panel.

nodes.role: Brass cobblestones in front of Holocaust victims' last homes. 100,000+ across Europe. You stumble on them. You look down. You read a name. You remember. The graph is a stumbling stone.

nodes.label: The Empty Chair at the Table
nodes.role: Thanksgiving. Christmas. The chair where someone used to sit. The desk in the classroom. The seat at graduation. The absence that speaks louder than presence.

nodes.label: The Last Witness

nodes.role: 1950: 1,849,568. 2020: 639,111. The city lost 2 out of every 3 people. The schools lost 2 out of every 3 students. The commons hollowed out. The people left. The buildings stayed.

nodes.role: 195 schools closed since 2005. Each one was a building. Each one was a community. Each one was a walk to school. Each closing is a neighborhood losing its center.

nodes.label: Detroit Literacy: 47% Functionally Illiterate
nodes.role: Nearly half of Detroit's adults cannot read well enough to fill out a job application. This is not an accident. This is the result. This is what 30 years of PA 362 produced.

nodes.label: Detroit Water Shutoffs: 141,000
nodes.role: 141,000 households had water shut off since 2014. Water. In a city surrounded by 21% of the world's freshwater. The commons denied to the people who live beside it.

nodes.label: 12th Street (1967 Rebellion)
nodes.role: 5 days. 43 dead. 1,189 injured. 7,231 arrested. 2,509 buildings burned. The city never recovered. The schools never recovered. The grief is 59 years old and still fresh.

nodes.label: The Promise That Was Detroit

nodes.label: The Teacher Who Stayed
nodes.role: Knew the school was failing. Knew the principal was lying. Stayed because the children needed someone. Stayed because leaving would be one more adult who left. The teacher who stayed is not complicit. The teacher who stayed is heartbroken.

nodes.label: The Janitor Who Saw Everything
nodes.role: Cleaned the hallways. Emptied the trash. Saw the empty classrooms. Saw the books that were never opened. Saw the children who stopped coming. Said nothing because nobody asked. Nobody ever asks the janitor.

nodes.label: The Secretary Who Filed the Reports
nodes.role: Typed the attendance numbers that were wrong. Filed the reports that were false. Didn't write them. Didn't approve them. But pressed send. Complicity by keystroke. Grief by employment.

nodes.label: The Bus Driver
nodes.role: Drove the route every morning. Picked up the children. Dropped them at the school. Drove the route every afternoon. Brought them home. Every day. Didn't know the school was a fraud. Drove the route.

nodes.label: The Lunch Lady
nodes.role: Fed the children. Sometimes the only meal they would eat that day. The child who asks for extra because there is nothing at home. The lunch lady gives extra. The lunch lady always gives extra.

nodes.label: The Grandparent Raising Grandchildren

nodes.role: Heat to red. Plunge into water. The thermal shock makes steel hard. Too fast: brittle. Too slow: soft. The investigation must be quenched at the right speed.

nodes.label: Tempering
nodes.role: After quenching, reheat gently. Makes steel tough without making it brittle. Strength with flexibility. The investigation must be tempered. Strong but not brittle.

nodes.label: Arc Welding
nodes.role: 6,500F. Electric arc melts metal. Two pieces become one. The joint is often stronger than the base metal. The connection the investigation makes is stronger than what was there before.

nodes.label: Forge Scale (Oxidation)

nodes.label: Damascus Steel

nodes.label: Ford Rouge Plant (1928)

nodes.label: Osmium (Densest Element)
nodes.role: 22.59 g/cm3. A cubic foot weighs 1,410 lbs. The densest natural element. The investigation is osmium. Dense with evidence. Heavy with truth.

nodes.label: Tungsten (Highest Melting Point)
nodes.role: 6,192F. Light bulb filaments. Armor-piercing rounds. The element that doesn't melt. The record that doesn't melt.

nodes.role: 1.7 grams can power a home for a year. Or destroy a city. The same material. Different intentions. Public money: education or extraction. Same dollar. Different purpose.

nodes.role: Deuterium instead of hydrogen. 10% heavier. Used in nuclear reactors. Looks like water. Tastes like water. Isn't water. Looks like a school. Acts like a school. Isn't a school.

nodes.label: Steel Belt to Rust Belt
nodes.role: Pittsburgh. Cleveland. Detroit. Gary. Youngstown. Flint. The cities that built America. The cities America abandoned. The schools that educated America. The schools America abandoned.

nodes.role: Molten metal poured into molds. The mold shapes the metal. The institution shapes the child. What happens when the mold is broken? What happens when the institution is fraudulent? Misshapen.

nodes.role: 11.2 km/s to leave Earth. The minimum speed to break free from gravity. The minimum evidence to break free from institutional capture. Are we at escape velocity?

nodes.label: Gravitational Lensing
nodes.role: Mass bends light. Massive objects distort the image of what's behind them. The institution bends the truth. The more massive the institution, the more distorted the truth behind it.

nodes.label: Tidal Locking
nodes.role: The moon always shows the same face. Locked by gravity. The institution always shows the same face. Locked by power. The dark side of the moon exists. The dark side of the institution exists.

nodes.label: Lagrange Points
nodes.role: 5 points where gravity from two bodies balances perfectly. A spacecraft can park there. The investigation parks at the Lagrange point between the institution and the public. Balanced. Stable. Watching.

nodes.label: Spaghettification (Black Holes)
nodes.role: Falling into a black hole: the gravity gradient stretches you into spaghetti. The institution stretches truth. The closer you get to the center of power, the more distorted everything becomes.

nodes.label: Gravitational Time Dilation
nodes.role: Clocks run slower in stronger gravity. Near the institution, time moves differently. The complaint filed 3 years ago feels like yesterday. The FOIA response takes forever. Time dilates near power.

nodes.label: Center of Mass
nodes.role: The point where the entire mass of a system can be treated as concentrated. Public Education: 2,879 edges. The center of mass of the graph. Everything orbits the commons.

nodes.label: Entropy of Accountability
nodes.role: Disorder always increases. Unless you add energy. The charter system tends toward disorder. The investigation adds energy. The filings are negative entropy. Order from effort.

nodes.label: Conservation of Energy
nodes.role: Energy cannot be created or destroyed. Only transformed. The harm done to 5,432 child-years cannot be destroyed. It was transformed. Into the investigation. Into the graph. Into the record.

nodes.label: Absolute Zero (-273.15C)
nodes.role: Molecular motion stops. Nothing moves. The institution at absolute zero: no oversight, no movement, no accountability. The AGC at -273.15 degrees of activity.

nodes.label: Latent Heat
nodes.role: The energy absorbed during phase change. Ice to water: absorbs heat but temperature doesn't rise. The institution absorbs complaints without changing. Absorbs and absorbs. Then suddenly: phase change.

nodes.label: Critical Temperature
nodes.role: Above this point, liquid and gas become indistinguishable. Above enough pressure, public and private education become indistinguishable. That's the point. That's the design.

nodes.label: Black Body Radiation
nodes.role: A perfect absorber emits a perfect spectrum. The institution that absorbs all complaints emits a perfect silence. The spectrum of silence.

nodes.label: Carnot Efficiency
nodes.role: The maximum possible efficiency of a heat engine. No real engine reaches it. No real institution reaches perfect accountability. But Carnot tells you the theoretical maximum. Aim there.

nodes.label: Tim Cook (Apple)
nodes.role: Apple CEO. $3T company. Public school: Robertsdale High, Alabama. Public education -> richest company on Earth.

nodes.label: Satya Nadella (Microsoft)
nodes.role: Microsoft CEO. From Hyderabad public school to $3T. Empathy as leadership. Hit Refresh.

nodes.label: Andy Jassy (Amazon)
nodes.role: Amazon CEO. Scarsdale public schools. $1.9T company built on public infrastructure: roads, internet, post offices.

nodes.label: Sundar Pichai (Google/Alphabet)
nodes.role: Grew up in Chennai. Two-room apartment. Public university in India. Now runs the world's information.

nodes.label: Jensen Huang (NVIDIA)
nodes.role: Semiconductor king. $3T company. Refugee from Taiwan. Oregon State public university. AI revolution.

nodes.label: Mark Zuckerberg (Meta)
nodes.role: Gave $100M to Newark schools. It failed. Didn't understand the system. Money without understanding is waste.

nodes.label: Elon Musk (Tesla/SpaceX/X)
nodes.role: Richest person. $230B+. Public schools in South Africa. Now wants to defund public education. The ladder he climbed, he wants to pull up.

nodes.label: Jamie Dimon (JPMorgan Chase)
nodes.role: Largest US bank. $4T in assets. Every charter school has a bank account. Every public dollar passes through a bank.

nodes.label: Warren Buffett (Berkshire)
nodes.role: Public schools in Omaha. Rose Hill Elementary. The richest investor. Public education made him.

nodes.label: Mary Barra (GM)
nodes.role: First woman CEO of a major automaker. Waterford Mott High School. Michigan public schools. GM is Detroit. Detroit is public schools.

nodes.label: Doug McMillon (Walmart)
nodes.role: Walmart CEO. Largest private employer. Walton family owns Walmart AND funds charter schools. The employer AND the defunder.

nodes.label: Bob Iger (Disney)
nodes.role: Disney CEO. Public schools in Long Island. The man who runs imagination went to public school.

nodes.label: Lisa Su (AMD)
nodes.role: MIT. Semiconductor pioneer. Born in Taiwan. Challenged NVIDIA. Public university pipeline.

nodes.label: Arvind Krishna (IBM)
nodes.role: IIT Kanpur. Public university India. Now runs IBM. The public education pipeline is global.

nodes.label: Brian Moynihan (Bank of America)
nodes.role: Public schools in Marietta, Ohio. Brown University. $3.2T in assets.
